messages.subject: model_header.hpp file not found
parts:
Issue 1.

I'm still getting

...
c++ src/test/mcmc/models/improper.cpp -Lbin -lstan -o src/test/mcmc/models/improper
src/test/mcmc/models/improper.cpp:3:10: fatal error: 'stan/model/model_header.hpp' file not found
#include <stan/model/model_header.hpp>
^
1 error generated.

This was just after running clean-all, then running test-unit, then
running test-unit again, all with CC+clang++ and O=0.

Does this have to do with precompiled headers? If so, can
we just drop the precompiled headers if they only save us
10% in compile time?


Issue 2.

I ran a second time because when I ran test-unit the first time, there wasn't
an error, but it also didn't end on running any tests -- it ended with
compiler warnings. Is that expected because of the concurrency?

No way I can scroll so far back up to find it, though,
so I'm running again from scratch so I can report errors if
I get the same behavior again.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] model_header.hpp file not found
parts:
I tracked down the issue. There was a file src/test/mcmc/models/improper.cpp
that wasn't under version control. When I got rid of it,
everything worked again.

Now I'm wondering where improper.cpp came from. It was a Stan
model translated to C++.

- Bob
